title: Append Mode

fakeFiles.story.txt:
Once upon a time.
A robot found a map.
The end.

goal: This lesson covers how append mode adds new text to the end of a file without erasing what is already there.
learn: Write more lines at the end
idea: Mode "a" means append. New text goes on the end and the old text stays. You write f = open("log.txt", "a") and then f.write("new line\n"). Use "w" to replace and "a" to add.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, add a third day by putting an extra line in the append write, or by adding another write before close, and press Run. You should see three days.

practice.text: Create memo.txt with "Hello\n" using "w", then append "Again\n", then print the file.
practice.hint: After the first close(), open memo.txt again with mode "a", write "Again\n", close it, and then read and print like the starter does.
practice.starterTip: Add: f = open("memo.txt", "a"), then f.write("Again\n"), then f.close() in the "# Append Again" section.
practice.starter:
f = open("memo.txt", "w")
f.write("Hello\n")
f.close()
# Append Again

f = open("memo.txt")
print(f.read())
f.close()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if memo has Hello and Again using append, then printed.

practice.text: Append one new tip line to tips.txt, then print the whole tips file.
practice.hint: tips.txt is already opened in append mode, so f.write() adds to the end. Put a \n on your tip so it gets its own line.
practice.starterTip: Try f.write("Take breaks when coding.\n") or any short tip you like, then run and check all tips print.
practice.starter:
f = open("tips.txt", "a")
f.write()
f.close()
f = open("tips.txt")
print(f.read())
f.close()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if tips.txt grows by one line via append and is printed.

quiz.question: What does mode "a" do?

options.text: Erases the whole file first always

quiz.wrong: Mode a adds to the end of the file.

quiz.question: How is "a" different from "w"?
quiz.correct: Yes, "w" replaces and "a" keeps what was there.
quiz.wrong: Write against append is the key idea.

quiz.question: After appending, does the first line still exist?
quiz.correct: Right, old lines stay when you append.

project.title: Practice Log
project.desc: Write a first log line with w, append two more days with a, and then print the full log.
project.starter:
f = open("practice_log.txt", "w")
f.write("Day 1\n")
f.close()
# Append Day 2 and Day 3

f = open("practice_log.txt")

f.close()
